title: Canonical finite coefficient comparisons in purity coordinates
statement: In the setting of [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts], define the pullback coefficient comparison by the scalar-adjunction mate of the exact restriction/pullback square [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], conjugated by the canonical intrinsic-realization comparison. The comparison on $Lf^*K(d)[2d]$ is the unique isomorphism that, in every pair of primitive-root charts related by $\zeta_m=\zeta_n^{\ell^{n-m}}$, becomes this pullback comparison and the canonical shift comparison. For separated finite-type schemes, define the compact-support comparison [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] as the scalar adjunct of compact support of the scalar unit followed by the canonical proper/open restriction comparison. The exceptional comparison [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is the unique arrow whose compact-support transpose is the reduced counit of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. Use the exceptional realization coordinates of [thm-pur-composition-coherence]. The coefficient-unit comparison is the scalar adjunct of the degree-zero coefficient map, fixed on all ring sections. These are the six-operation finite-reduction maps, rather than arbitrary endpoint isomorphisms.
